title: Listening & Reading
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata untuk mendeskripsikan pakaian dan struktur untuk menanyakan harga pakaian.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 51-53
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to understand and identify additional key vocabulary about clothes (long, short, a floral skirt, a pretty dress, athletic shorts, striped socks).
Learners will listen and understand people talking about clothes.
Learners will read and understand a text about going shopping.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures in Listening A on Student Book page 51.
Tell them that they need to listen and circle the correct word or phrase that they hear in the audio.
Before listening, practice pronunciation of the words in task A. The teacher says the two vocabulary choices given for each number, e.g. “Number 1. a. long. b. log.” and students repeat them.
Play audio 6.3. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check students’ understanding.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, play the audio again, and then check the answers together.

Play audio 6.3 again and ask students to write down the sentences they hear in their notebooks (this is a simple dictation activity). Then show the audio script and ask students to correct their sentences.
This activity is for pronunciation practice.

Play audio 6.4 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly (long, short, a floral skirt, a pretty dress, athletic shorts, striped socks), and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
In order to make vocabulary drilling more interesting, students could be guided to drill using different emotions (e.g. excited or surprised) or voices.
Ask students to look at listening task C. Put students in pairs and ask them to describe what the six children are wearing (e.g. “She is wearing a pretty yellow dress.”).
After 3-4 minutes, elicit ideas from the students.
Read the names aloud (Chris, Max, Sam, Abby, Florence, Jenny) and ask students to repeat them, so they are prepared to hear the names in the audio.
Tell students that they need to listen and draw lines from each name to the student who matches that description.
Play audio 6.5. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, play the audio again, and check the answers together on the board.
If there is time, show audio script 6.5 and ask students to read the sentences aloud in pairs (Student A reads 1, 3, 5 and Student B reads 2, 4, 6, then switch), paying attention to intonation.
Ask students to look at the pictures on Student Book page 52-53 and ask, “What can you see on the page?”
Ask some specific questions about the pictures, for example, ‘How many people can you see?’, ‘Where are they?’
Giving some personal questions is also suggested to make it more relatable to students, for example, “Do you like going shopping for clothes?”
Ask students to look at task A on Student Book page 52 (new vocabulary: light, dark, jeans, shirt).
Say the new vocabulary and ask students to repeat after you.
Tell students that the first sentence in each box relates to the picture on the left, and the second sentence is a question they answer by looking at the two pictures on the right.
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do. Then put students in pairs to complete the task in around 5 minutes.
Check the answers as a class and write them on the board.
For extra practice, point to objects in the classroom and ask students if they are light coloured or dark coloured.

Ask students to look at task B on Student Book page 52. Put students in pairs and ask them to discuss the questions (e.g. “What are your favourite clothes to wear?”, “Is your school uniform light or dark?”, “Can you wear jeans to school?”).
Give students 3-5 minutes to complete the task.
Then ask some students to share their answers with the class. Answers will vary because these questions require students' own personal responses.
Tell students that they will listen and read the story. Play audio 6.6 and ask them to read the text silently.
Next, play audio 6.6 again and ask students to read the text aloud, following the audio. Ask if there are any questions about the language in the text.

As a way to make the reading session more engaging, teachers could divide the class into several groups and assign each group to read one paragraph alternately in different ways (e.g. loudly or quietly).
Ask students to look at task D on Student Book page 53.
Tell students to circle the correct word to complete each sentence about the story (e.g. light or dark, jacket or shirt, like or likes).
The first question can be done together as a class to make sure students know what to do.
Then, they can complete the task in pairs or by themselves.
Ask students to check their answers with a friend.
Check the answers as a class. Write the answers on the board and read the correct sentences aloud together.
Now ask students to look at task E (e.g. “Who do you like to go shopping with? Why?”, “Which new clothes do you want to buy? Why?”).
Instruct them to discuss the questions in groups of three or four students.
After about 6-8 minutes, elicit some answers for each question from each group. Encourage students to give a reason using “because”.
This activity could be done if there is more time.
Ask students to write two of their own multiple choice questions about the reading text in their notebooks. Each question should have three or four answer options (a, b, c or a, b, c, d).

Put students in pairs and ask them to answer each other’s questions. They can read the text again if needed. Then, each student says whether the answer is correct or incorrect (“Yes, that’s correct.” / “No, that’s not correct.”) and explains why.
Ask around five individual students to write one of their multiple choice questions on the whiteboard.
Then ask the whole class to answer each question by holding up 1 finger for a, 2 fingers for b, 3 fingers for c, or 4 fingers for d.
The students who wrote the questions on the board should tell the class the correct answer and explain why.
Wrap up the class by asking the students which new clothes they would like to buy and why, using the new words (e.g. “I want to buy light blue jeans because they are comfortable.”).
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: ketepatan jawaban tugas listening (menomori/menjodohkan/melengkapi).
Pertanyaan pemahaman bacaan (literal & inferensial) dan pembahasan bersama.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
